$comment: Schema for the TorchStone Executive Protection dashboard. Mirrors the SEA dashboard's schema.json as a design/reference document -- index.html is hand-built to match this shape (the shell is not a runtime schema loader), so treat this file as the source of truth to keep code and config in sync when the dataset evolves.

dataSource.$comment: Single global dataset -- no country split, so the SEA-style multi-source country-nav + dimmed background layers are dropped entirely rather than configured with one entry.

columns.name: Location
columns.$comment: Derived during export from City, State/Province, Country -- not a raw XLSX column.

defaultFocus.$comment: On load, the map fits bounds to USA rows (largest share of the sample data) while still plotting all global incidents.

layers.label: Tactic
layers.$comment: 'Other Crime' has zero current incidents in the sample data but is pre-defined here so it appears in filters/legend/table pills as soon as it's used.

layers.label: Metrics
layers.$comment: Rendered as an always-visible bottom-left panel (not a map-toggle tab, unlike SEA), split from the map by its own adjustable divider. Unlike SEA's fixed chart list, this is a single vertical (stacked) bar chart with one user-facing selector: 'Break down by' (inline with the chart title), which adds an optional second dimension -- stacked segments colored by that field's own color map. The x-axis grouping is NOT a separate control; it always mirrors whichever map layer tab is currently active (Target/Tactic/Venue). Both the implicit group-by and the breakdown selector are restricted to those three categorical layers. The chart canvas has a repeating diagonal TorchStone Global watermark tiled across the plot area background (low opacity, drawn behind the bars) and a small icon-only Copy button pinned to the card's top-right corner that copies the chart image to the clipboard (falls back to a PNG download if the browser doesn't support clipboard image writes).
layers.groupBy: implicit -- always equals the active map layer

layers.label: Metrics Builder
layers.$comment: 4th layer tab. Unlike the other three, selecting it replaces BOTH the map and the single metrics chart with one full-height panel (the map/metrics divider is hidden too) -- it is not a map coloring layer. Lets the user build an open-ended grid of charts (2 per row, capped grid with scroll) instead of the single fixed metrics chart. Each chart has its own Chart Type / X Axis / Break Down By selection, chosen from all five categorical fields (Target, Tactic, Venue, Country, Domestic/Int'l) -- a superset of the three the map/metrics chart is restricted to. Y axis is shown as a fixed, disabled 'Count of Incidents' label rather than a real selector, since this dataset has no numeric measure column (unlike SEA's Arms Score) for a Y axis to meaningfully choose between. Charts respect the current table filters (date range, multi-selects, search) and re-render when they change, but only while this panel is actually visible (rebuilding a Chart.js canvas inside a display:none container sizes it to zero). Nothing here persists across a page reload by design -- the grid resets each session.
layers.yAxis: Count of Incidents (fixed -- no numeric measure column exists in this dataset)
